patch_description: The previous program failed validation for multiple structural reasons: (1) it never produced valid per-row `column_orderings` (always returned `[]`); (2) the recursive `itertuples`/attribute-based row manipulation corrupted/mixed rows, reset indices, appended an `original_index` column, dropped and merged columns, and finally re-sorted rows — so the returned DataFrame lost row identity and cell alignment; (3) the old squared-field-length heuristic (len**2) does not match the actual objective (character-prefix Trie reuse, measurable as the sum of LCPs between lexicographically adjacent serialized rows). The fix is a full rewrite: serialize each cell exactly as the evaluator does (missing -> "", otherwise str), construct at most three cheap whole-program candidates — (a) a global frequency-ranked column ordering using sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), (b) a bounded conditional partition tree that gives per-row orderings by recursively choosing the length-weighted best repeated field, and (c) the original column order as a safe fallback — then select the winner by actually computing ideal Trie reuse via sorting the serialized row strings and summing adjacent LCP lengths (binary-search prefix comparison, C-speed). All cell values, rows, and columns are preserved exactly; col_merge groups are kept contiguous as ordered units; the returned DataFrame keeps its original column order and index, and `column_orderings` contains one valid ordering per row consistent with the returned data.
